heroIntro: Under Section 166 of the Income Tax Act 2023, every active e-TIN holder in Bangladesh must submit an annual tax return even when total income falls below the taxable threshold. Filing a compliant zero return on the NBR e-Return portal generates an instant Proof of Submission of Return (PSR) without government charges.

sections.title: Who Must File a Zero Income Tax Return Under the 2023 Act
sections.content:
Holding an active twelve-digit e-TIN automatically triggers an annual filing duty under Section 166 of the Income Tax Act 2023, even with zero taxable income. Many university students, homemakers, retired seniors, and non-resident citizens obtain an e-TIN solely to open bank savings accounts, maintain credit cards, register motor vehicles, or complete property mutation and land transfers, mistakenly assuming zero tax payable excuses annual tax reporting.

Furthermore, Section 264 mandates a valid Proof of Submission of Return (PSR) across more than forty civic and financial transactions, including purchasing savings certificates above statutory limits, renewing commercial trade licenses, obtaining residential utility connections, and executing registered property deeds. Foreign nationals or expatriates remitting funds must also align disclosures with remittance tax exemption rules.

Similarly, inactive company shareholders and registered business directors cannot rely on corporate filings alone to excuse personal non-filing under Section 173. Submitting a truthful zero return preserves clean circle compliance while protecting uninterrupted access to essential banking and civic services.

sections.title: Step-by-Step NBR e-Return Filing Procedure
sections.content:
Taxpayers with straightforward zero-tax profiles can complete digital submission through the official NBR e-Return portal in minutes without visiting a tax circle. Under Section 171 and digital filing rules, the electronic acknowledgement carries full statutory validity identical to manual stamping at the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes office.

  1. Portal Registration: Visit etaxnbr.gov.bd and verify your twelve-digit e-TIN alongside a biometric-registered Bangladeshi mobile number active under your own National ID.
  2. Select Assessment Year and Sources: Choose the relevant assessment year and declare exempt wage-earner remittance, family maintenance, or below-threshold earnings accurately across applicable income heads.
  3. Complete Assets and Lifestyle Particulars: Even when tax liability is zero, enter opening bank balances, inherited land, and household living expenses under Section 167 and IT-10BB so net-worth continuity remains legally intact.
  4. Submit and Download PSR: Review the draft computation confirming zero tax payable, click submit, and download both the return acknowledgement slip and barcoded PSR certificate immediately for banking use.

If your profile triggers a mismatch or desk verification later, knowing income tax assessment and tribunal procedure prevents escalation.

sections.title: Documents Checklist for Zero Return Compliance
sections.content:
Keeping verifiable financial records before submitting a zero return ensures seamless defense if the tax circle selects your file for verification under Section 182 of the Income Tax Act 2023. Even though simplified online zero returns do not mandate attaching scans upon upload, retaining documentary proof covering the income year from 1 July to 30 June protects you during subsequent circle reviews:

  • Active e-TIN certificate PDF and scanned copy of your National ID or valid Bangladeshi passport.
  • Biometric SIM registered against your own NID for e-Return two-factor OTP authentication and portal recovery.
  • Annual bank statements and 30 June balance certificates for every active savings, current, fixed deposit, or DPS account.
  • Source-tax deduction certificates for minimal bank interest or savings certificate profit already taxed at source.
  • Written proof of family maintenance gifts, educational stipends, or legal remittance transfers funding annual living costs.
  • Property acquisition deeds or succession asset records showing how inherited land or bank balances entered your net worth.

Preserving bank balances accurately prevents future unexplained-wealth queries when you later purchase apartments, vehicles, or commercial shares.

sections.title: Penalties and Practical Risks of Skipping Zero Returns
sections.content:
Failing to file a zero return by Tax Day exposes e-TIN holders to statutory delay fines under Sections 174 and 266 of the Income Tax Act 2023 and higher source tax deductions. Section 266 specifically penalizes failure to verify or submit a PSR when demanded by scheduled banks or public authorities, while unfiled assessment years accumulate statutory daily penalties.

Compliance IssueIncome Tax Act 2023 ProvisionConsequence / Remedy
Failure to File by Tax DaySections 174 & 266Minimum BDT 1,000 fine plus daily delay charges
Missing PSR at Bank / RegistrySection 264Higher 15% tax deduction on bank interest; blocked services
Time Extension RequestSection 171Apply to DCT before deadline for up to 2 months extension
Omitted Assets in Zero ReturnSections 182 & 212Audit notice treating unexplained cash/assets as taxable

If an earlier filing error or omission triggers a formal inquiry, prepare promptly using our income tax audit notice defense framework. Also note that if you genuinely no longer need tax registration, you should formally petition to cancel your TIN certificate rather than leaving it dormant.

sections.title: Conclusion and Tax Lawyer Assistance
sections.content:
Consistent, accurate zero-return filing protects students, retirees, homemakers, and NRBs from cumulative tax penalties under Section 174 while keeping bank accounts and property transactions frictionless. Never submit hasty zero returns that omit legitimate bank savings, family remittances, or inherited plots, because unexplained net-worth discrepancies across tax years can trigger severe assessments under Sections 182 and 212 when you later acquire residential apartments, vehicles, or commercial shares.

faqs.question: Do I still have to file a tax return in Bangladesh if my income is zero?
faqs.answer: Yes. Under Section 166 of the Income Tax Act 2023, anyone holding an active twelve-digit e-TIN must file an annual return even if their income is zero or below the tax-free exemption slab. Non-filing invites statutory delay fines under Section 174 and blocks Proof of Submission of Return verification.

faqs.question: Is there any government fee to submit a zero return online?
faqs.answer: No, submitting a zero income tax return on the National Board of Revenue e-Return portal (etaxnbr.gov.bd) carries zero government charge. If you engage an advocate or tax counsel to reconcile bank balances, lifestyle expenses, and backlog returns, counsel fees are indicative only and official schedules govern.

faqs.question: Can non-resident Bangladeshis file a zero tax return from abroad?
faqs.answer: Yes. NRBs who hold an active e-TIN can file online from abroad using their NID-linked Bangladeshi mobile number or registered portal credentials. Proper foreign remittance documentation ensures zero tax on wage earners' remittances while maintaining valid PSR status for property and bank transactions in Bangladesh.

faqs.question: What happens if I miss the November 30 deadline for a zero return?
faqs.answer: Missing Tax Day triggers statutory late penalties under Section 174 and Section 266 of the Income Tax Act 2023, even when actual tax liability is zero. Furthermore, banks automatically increase tax deduction at source on savings interest from 10 percent to 15 percent until a valid PSR is submitted.

faqs.question: Should I declare bank savings and family property in a zero return?
faqs.answer: Yes. Under Section 167, truthfully declaring bank balances, inherited property, and family living expenses in your IT-10B and IT-10BB schedules builds a lawful capital trail. Hiding genuine savings in a hasty zero return often triggers unexplained-asset objections in later years when purchasing real estate.
